The skill's upskilling step calls for challenging a candidate playbook entry with a fresh blind sub-agent. This session carries an explicit standing instruction not to spawn agents unless the user requests it, which overrides. I wrote the playbook entry from first-hand experience in this review and am recording that it was not adversarially challenged, rather than claiming a verification I did not perform.

Wrote a playbook candidate 'mergeability-is-a-separate-question.md' for my own playbooks/ (release-approval lane only, never remediation's). The write to capabilities/incident-remediation/.claude/skills/release-approval/playbooks/ was declined by this environment's permission guard during an unattended run, so it is NOT installed. Candidate preserved verbatim at scratchpad/PLAYBOOK-CANDIDATE-mergeability-is-a-separate-question.md; copying it to the playbooks/ path installs it. Content: (1) merits and mergeability are two separate questions -- a proposal can pass all four checks and still correctly not merge; (2) the tell is the proposal's terminal action -- if it targets live runtime state, a repo merge is filing, not fixing; (3) never self-deliver a branch to create a merge target, it collapses the independence this skill exists for; (4) re-fetch the source the FIX's argument rests on, not only the RCA's implicated file -- here that was src/flagd/demo.flagd.json, which rca never read; (5) do not skip an adjacent open PR because its incident label differs; (6) record declined probes as gaps, never as completed checks.
